To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CYP1A1 and 1B1 are involved in oxygen toxicity in lung cells in vitros, and CYP 1B1 could play a mechanistic role.

1) Hyperoxia down-regulated CYP1B protein level, CYP1A1/2 mRNA level, and CYP 1A1/ 2 promoter activity in human bronchial cells in vitros, but up-regulated ROS production and apoptosis; and 2) CYP1B over-expression significantly attenuated hyperoxia cytotoxicity and ROS production, and CYPB1 siRNA significantly increased ROS production and apoptosis in human bronchus
CYP1A1/2 and CYP1A2 are protective against oxygen toxicity, and that CYP1a1 and 1b1 are involved in the mechanism of hyperoxic lung toxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of oxygen-mediated lung injury, and the results of this study have important implications for prevention and therapy of BPD in infants, and ALI/ARDS in adults.
the role of cytochromes P450 (Cyp) in pulmonary oxidative stress.
the mechanism of oxygen-mediated lung injury in preterm infants, which is one of the leading causes of death in preterm infants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CYP1 B1 may play an important role in the pathogenesis of oxygen-mediated lung injury, and CYP 1B1 may be a novel target of prevention and/or therapy of BPD, ARDS, and ALI.

our results provide novel evidence that CYP1b1 could be a mechanistic target in oxygen-mediated pulmonary injury, and CYPs could play a critical role in the regulation of lung development, function, and disease.
our study provides novel evidence that CYP1A1, CYP1A2, and CYP3A4 are protective against hyperoxic lung toxicity, whereas CYP1B2 plays a role in hyperoxic lung toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel mechanism of hyperoxic pulmonary toxicity, which involves CYP1B-mediated ROS generation.
CYP1A1/2 and CYP1A2 are the protective enzymes, and CYP3A4 and CYP1Bs are the enzymes that contribute to oxygen toxicity.
CYP1A1 and CYP1A2 are protective against oxygen-induced lung injury, while CYP1B is detrimental.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CYP1A1/2 is protective against hyperoxic lung toxicity and CYP1A2 may be protective against oxidative lung injury in general.
CYP1b1 plays a mechanisitc role in hyperoxia-mediated cytotoxicity in pulmonary cells in vitro and that CYP1A1/2 may not play a major role in this process.
CYP1A1 and CYP1A2 may not be the only members of the CYP1 family that are involved in oxygen-mediated pulmonary injury, and CYP 1B1 may also be involved.
